customize.text:
More than five hundred years ago, a young warrior named Burkina lived among the Scions of the Canopy. He was friends with the future Pyro Archon, Mavuika, since childhood, and was the first among them to receive the Ancient Name
This name was considered the most honorable in the tribe, but Mavuika declared that she would receive an even better Ancient Name —
Two thousand years earlier, this name belonged to the hero Yupanqui, who helped the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, reclaim Natlan from the dragons and then helped overthrow the tyrant of the Cinder City. Although the name Malipo is considered the most honored in Huitztlan, every bearer of this name died of unnatural causes. Some researchers even believed bearers were haunted by the specter of the Turnfire and that a higher power existed that constantly watched the name-bearer, studying their actions and ultimately demanding payment. examining their actions and eventually demanding payment in return. None can escape this payment — unless, perhaps, they could honestly swear by Turnfire to never make a single mistake in their entire life.

When Burkina was a young courier, he once made a bet with a Yumkasaurus who lived beyond the mountains that he could climb the farthest peak of Coatepec Mountain and harvest the Flamegranates from the mother tree, which grew higher than the volcano. Burkina could scale the highest cliff, clinging to the ledges with bare hands, but he was no match for the Saurians and animals circling above the peak and sitting beneath the tree, waiting for the fruit. Rather than give in to despair, the young courier set out to train. In Tlalocan, he studied the Qucusaurs; in Teteocan, he honed his body with great boulders; and in Mictlan, he learned to expand his consciousness and sharpen his perception. During these training sessions, his friend Tenoch, who had grown long hair, spotted Burkina and offered him company. Burkina knew that the practice he was dedicating himself to was a necessary price for the goal he sought to achieve, and his friend's kindness might not be without reciprocity. Seeing his friend determined to pursue his path alone, Tenoch didn't insist but offered to forge a weapon together.
When the Flamegranates were ripe, the young courier slung the forged hooked sword over his shoulder and cut across the cliffs. He easily repelled the attacks of the winged Saurians, and all that remained was to swing the hook to harvest the Flamegranates hanging from the tree. But just before victory, Burkina's pride made him complacent, and a sudden gust of wind threw him back. He was about to fall from a great height when a Yumkasaurus suddenly appeared in the dense canopy of the mother tree and saved the courier from death with its long tongue. The same Yumkasaurus who always tussled with Burkina secretly followed him and saved him at a crucial moment. The young courier gave him the Flamegranates as a token of gratitude, and thus began a friendship between the future hero of Natlan and the Mountain King Kongamato.

When a dark wave spread across Natlan, Burkina's friend Tenoch set out to unite the warring and squabbling tribes. Burkina and Kongamato voluntarily joined the exiled warrior, believing it better to shed blood for fiery justice than to rot on a comfortable bed of grass. In addition to the young warrior, Tenoch was joined by five other heroes from five other tribes. All bore the Ancient Names of the first Archon Xbalanque's companions. Together, they fought in a battle that created the Mare Jivari. During the Cataclysm, the Mountain King was infected by the Abyss and lost his mind. In a fit of madness, he attacked Burkina, but the latter did not resist, choosing instead to call upon the power of the Turnfire at the cost of his own life and transfer it to Kongamato. Perhaps he believed the Mountain King was stronger than him and more valuable to the tribe, or perhaps he acted out of loyalty to his friend. When the time came for Pyro Archon's plan to be carried out, Burkina's spirit helped the heir of his Ancient Name, Kinich, give Haborym power to fight the Abyss.

After Burkina's death during the Cataclysm, Huitztlan began to maintain the peace of the Mountain King, who had fallen into hibernation. The memories of his friend were lost to a long nightmare, and even the name "Kongamato" itself has become unfamiliar to the ancient lord of the Yumkasaurs. The Abyss energy within him was extremely sensitive, and if disturbed, he would awaken and fly into a blind rage, attacking anything that moved. The Mountain King was unable to break free from the nightmare, but he had to protect the Turnfire, no longer even knowing to whom it belonged. Even if the great body he was once so proud of continues to be wracked by burning agony, even if his now decaying frame still bears the imprints of unbearable shame, even so, he would never allow anyone to desecrate the life and fire that were once his. For the giant beast, now lost to madness, despite his soul having been consumed by the filth of darkness, this final shred of resolve he refused to abandon, no matter what.

<color=#ffffffd9>"I shall return the Turnfire name to the Night Realm, in exchange for the final kindling."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"By past fuel, and present flame, life marches ever on."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"We will answer to the fire for all our deeds. Amidst the flames, we shall be reunited."</color>

The tribe started celebrating a ceremony, the Turnfire Night, during which they remembered the fallen hero of Natlan and cleansed the Abyss within the Mountain King so that he would remain soundly asleep. Over time, Abyssal activity in Natlan increased, affecting the unstable energy within the Yumkasaurus, causing him to awaken and attack with increasing frequency. Some elders decided to completely purge Kongamato of the Abyss, which would have resulted in the death of the tribe's symbol, but the current bearer of the Malipo name, Kinich, was able to restore the Yumkasaurus's sanity. The Flame of Turning, summoned by the Mountain King himself, and the Sacred Flame created a transparent shell around Kongamato, isolating him from the external influence of the Abyss.
